title: CaseGraphen MCP host: reconcile_verification_lineage payload
description: The literal `payload.verification_lineage` an MCP client sends for the `reconcile_verification_lineage` tool. Each `anchors[]` entry's `anchor_id` is caller-chosen and must be unique and non-empty within the request; `policy.required_anchors` lists the anchor_id values the lineage must supply, matched by id, not by kind. `kind` instead selects how the host independently re-derives that anchor's proof rather than trusting the caller's assertion.

retained_lineage_files.description: Local paths to the retained producer artifacts the host reads to independently re-derive the lineage proof. Not reused elsewhere in the codebase; carried only as `producer_files`.

verification_anchor_input.description: Not reused elsewhere in the codebase; carried only as an item of `anchors`. `kind` selects which independent proof the host derives — the caller's other fields identify what to check, not what the check found.

artifact_id.description: Required, and only accepted, when kind is case_artifact. Must equal artifact:sha256-<hash of artifact_path's bytes>; see this anchor's case_artifact branch below for the full check.

artifact_path.description: Required, and only accepted, when kind is case_artifact.

then.description: The host derives this anchor's proof from the execution trace named in producer_files.execution_trace_path; no further fields are accepted.

The host derives this anchor's proof by simultaneously checking three things against artifact_path's bytes: (1) artifact_id equals artifact:sha256-<hash> of those bytes; (2) a case cell with id artifact_id exists in the ledger, is of custom type "artifact", is in lifecycle Resolved or Accepted, and carries metadata.content_hash equal to the same hash; (3) the case space itself evaluates as canonically valid. Any mismatch across those three refuses the anchor — it is not three independent optional checks.
